methodological_rigor.justification: The local normalized manuscript contains only the title, '[Retracted] Clinical significance of bromodomain-containing protein 7 and its association with tumor progression in prostate cancer,' and no abstract, methods, results, or statistical analysis. Because no study design, sample, controls, endpoints, assays, or analyses are provided, methodological rigor cannot be substantiated from the manuscript text. The retracted status in the title further precludes treating the scientific claims as reliable. No statistical approach or results are present to evaluate.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Only a retracted title about BRD7 and prostate cancer progression is available in the local manuscript file. No design, patient population, endpoint, intervention, or outcome is reported, so the highest supportable Oxford classification is 5 because the evidence cannot be classified as an evaluable clinical study from the available text. The topic could be clinically relevant in principle, but no clinical or translational evidence is available in the normalized corpus. The retraction label prevents assigning meaningful practice or translational impact.

reporting_quality.justification: No reporting standard can be applied because the file provides only a retracted title and no manuscript content. There are no methods, inclusion criteria, sample descriptions, outcomes, figures, tables, ethics statements, or statistical details in the normalized text. No data availability, code availability, repository, or supplementary protocol is described. The available record therefore has essentially no reproducible reporting content.

novelty_literature.justification: The available text contains only a retracted title, so there is no introduction, gap statement, comparator literature, findings, or mechanistic argument to assess. Any claim about BRD7's clinical significance in prostate cancer cannot be evaluated from the provided file. The retracted label also undermines any novelty claim that might have existed in the original article. On the available manuscript evidence, no new reliable knowledge is demonstrated.

There is no scientific narrative or presentation to evaluate beyond the retraction-labelled title. The absence of content prevents assessment of clarity, organization, captions, or citation quality.
